events.title: Professional Science Master's in Environmental Policy and Management Seminar
events.description: Title: How journalism can move audiences from awareness to action through community-centered storytelling by Dr. Yulia Strokova, founder and publisher of Impact.Edition Abstract Featured Discussion How can journalism move people from awareness to action? Drawing on her experience as the founder and publisher of Impact.Edition, Dr. Yulia Strokova will explore how solutions-focused journalism can spotlight credible responses to social and environmental challenges while remaining rigorous, critical, and independent. Through Miami-based examples, she will discuss how journalists can center community voices, examine evidence of impact, and avoid simplistic “hero narratives.” She will also demonstrate how stories can extend beyond the page through public exhibitions, print publications, newsletters, events, and partnerships, reaching new audiences and creating opportunities for participation. The presentation invites emerging journalists to think beyond documenting problems and consider how thoughtful, community-centered storytelling can inspire community engagement and drive meaningful action.

events.title: THE ADAPTIVE HOME: A Book Talk with Professor Sam Moshaver.
events.description: You are invited to hear Dr. Sam Moshaver talk about his new book: The Adaptive Home: Supplementary Space Design for an Uncertain Future. The book provides a comprehensive guide for architects, urban planners, and developers on designing and retrofitting residential environments to meet the evolving needs of residents. About the Author Dr. Sam Moshaver is an Assistant Professor of Interior Architecture in the School of Architecture at Florida International University. He also serves as co-director of the Collaboratory for Design Environment & Cognition (CODEC) Lab, where his empirical research investigates environment-behavior studies, neuroinclusive design, and spatial comfort.

events.description: Are you providing the best context to your AI to get the results you are looking for? events.title: LA HORA DEL CAFÉ
events.host: Maurice A. Ferré Institute for Civic Leadership, Spanish Resource Center
events.description: LA HORA DEL CAFÉ La Hora del Café is a weekly conversation and community-building event hosted by the Department of Modern Languages at Florida International University (FIU) . The event provides students, faculty, and language enthusiasts with an informal and welcoming environment to practice Spanish, strengthen intercultural communication skills, and connect with members of the FIU community. Held every Tuesday from 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Department of Modern Languages (SIPA II, Room 216), La Hora del Café encourages participants of all proficiency levels to engage in spontaneous conversations in Spanish while enjoying complimentary coffee and pastries sponsored by Café Bustelo . The initiative supports the department's mission of promoting language learning beyond the classroom by creating authentic opportunities for oral communication, cultural exchange, and community engagement. Through relaxed conversation and peer interaction, participants develop confidence in their Spanish-speaking abilities, expand their cultural awareness, and build meaningful connections with fellow students and faculty. From Tuesday, September 29, 2026 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM EDT at SIPA II 216 .

events.title: Calming the Storm: Utilizing CALM for Early Childhood Anxiety
events.description: Date: Thursday, October 1st & Friday, October 2nd, 2026 Time: 9 a.m. - 1 p.m. ET (each day) Format: Live virtual training (link and access details will be provided upon registration) Cost: $250 for professionals / $50 for students Register here: https://redcap.fiu.edu/surveys/?s=DJHLHK7W8XWJNNF7 About the Talk: Enhance your clinical toolkit for treating early childhood anxiety through this dynamic, interactive workshop on one of the adaptations of Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT). Focusing on the Coaching Approach behavior and Leading by Modeling (CALM) model, the workshop integrates didactic instruction, live demonstrations, video examples, role plays, and interactive activities to build a strong foundation in PCIT skills for anxiety. Participants will learn PRIDE skills, along with exposure-based strategies and parent coaching techniques to actively engage caregivers and support the generalization of gains beyond the therapy setting. Attendees will leave with a practical, hands-on toolkit to help caregivers shift from “rescuing” to “empowering” their child, transforming the parent-child relationship into a powerful driver of brave, flexible behavior. This presentation targets psychologists, clinicians, trainees, and students, offering content at a beginner/intermediate level. The speakers have reported no conflicts of interest or commercial support for this talk. Learning Objectives: 1.Describe multiple etiologies and trajectory for early childhood anxiety. 2.Identify 3 behavioral strategies (e.g., positive reinforcement, parent coaching, exposure) used in treating anxiety in young children. 3.Define the Child-Directed Interaction (CDI) skills and DADS skills necessary in PCIT-CALMfor early childhood anxiety. 4.Use the adapted PCIT methods in their clinical practice with youth with anxiety for greater overall care. About the Speakers: Dr. Jami Furr is a Clinical Associate Professor and Senior Psychologist in the Mental Health Interventions and Novel Therapeutics (MINT) Program, and Developer of the Selective Mutism Program at the Center for Children and Families (CCF) at Florida International University. Dr. Furr has extensive expertise in cognitive-behavioral treatments of childhood anxiety, trauma, and disruptive behavior disorders, with a particular focus on preschool mental health and children with selective mutism. She served as the Clinical Director and Supervisor for several federally and foundation-funded trials on adaptations of Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT), including the Internet-delivered Coaching Approach behavior and Learning by Modeling (CALM) program for young children with anxiety and the intensive group behavioral treatment for selective mutism (IGBT-SM). Dr. Furr also directed one of the first long-term outcome studies on youth with SM. She is the Past-President of the Selective Mutism Association and has continued to serve on their Board of Directors for the last 9 years. Dr. Furr currently provides training and supervision of graduate students conducting clinical services for anxiety, selective mutism, OCD, and/or disruptive behavior problems in youth. Carolina Costa is a Licensed Mental Health Counselor and Clinic Coordinator in the MINT Program at the Center for Children and Families (CCF) at Florida International University. Carolina has extensive clinical experience providing cognitive-behavioral treatment for childhood anxiety, with a particular focus on children and adolescents with selective mutism. She is bilingual in English and Spanish and provides clinical services in both languages. Carolina has experience providing individual and group-based interventions, as well as intensive services for children and adolescents. Her clinical experience also includes collaborating with teachers and school personnel through teacher consultation and providing in-classroom interventions to support children in applying treatment skills across school and other real-world settings. She additionally assists with the training and supervision of graduate students providing clinical services for anxiety, selective mutism, OCD, and disruptive behavior problems in youth. Carolina has served as the coordinator for clinical research studies, including the Kids Face-to-face And Computer-Enhanced Formats Effectiveness study for Anxiety and Related Symptoms (Kids FACE FEARS) and the Selective Mutism Intervention Long-term Evaluation (SMILE).

events.title: Women, Violence and Memory: The Human Legacy of the Partition of British India
events.host: Steven J Green School of International & Public Affairs, Václav Havel Program for Human Rights & Democracy
events.description: The 1947 Partition of British India triggered one of the largest forced migrations in modern history, uprooting millions and transforming communities across the subcontinent. Women experienced this upheaval in profoundly gendered ways, facing abduction, sexual violence, displacement and the loss of family and home. This conversation explores women’s experiences of Partition and the memories carried across generations, examining how recovering often-silenced histories can deepen our understanding of violence, survival, displacement and the enduring human consequences of Partition. This event is presented as part of the programming for the exhibition Project Dastaan, currently on view in the Green School Gallery (SIPA I, Room 110).

events.title: Period Talks: Real Talk, Real Cost
events.host: Centers for Student Engagement, Women's Center
events.description: Period Talks: Real Talk, Real Cost The Women’s Center will facilitate a discussion addressing pink tax and its impact on affordability and access to quality products and services. The pink tax refers to the higher prices often charged for products and services marketed towards women compared to similar items aimed at men. This phenomenon is not a formal tax but rather a pricing disparity observed in various consumer goods, including toiletries, clothing, and even personal services. For instance, studies have shown that items like women's razors and shampoos can be more expensive than their male counterparts, despite being nearly identical in function. The term "pink tax" is derived from the association of the color pink with femininity, leading to the notion that products tailored for women often carry a premium. The conversation will focus on understanding pink tax, period equity, and women’s reproductive health given current legislation. Need an accommodation or accessible materials? events.title: Bringing Skills into Action: Rethinking Engagement and Treatment Delivery for Youth and Adolescents with ADHD
events.description: About the speaker: Melissa R. Dvorsky, Ph.D., is a psychologist and Associate Professor at Children’s National Hospital and the George Washington University School of Medicine where she directs the ADHD & Learning Differences Program. She has authored over 70 peer-reviewed publications on ADHD with research funded by the National Institute of Mental Health and the U.S. Department of Education Institute of Education Sciences. Dr. Dvorsky developed the Advanced Tools for Organization Management (ATOM), a technology-enhanced organizational skills intervention for adolescents with ADHD. She is an Associate Editor of the Journal of Attention Disorders and serves on the editorial boards for the Journal of Youth & Adolescence and School Mental Health. Dr. Dvorsky’s research is focused on partnering with communities including schools and care providers, to improve the access, effectiveness, and sustainability of services for the ADHD community. About the talk: Evidence-based interventions for adolescents with ADHD can effectively target organizational, time-management, and related functional skills, yet treatment outcomes depend on adolescents’ engagement and ability to use these strategies in everyday contexts. This presentation will examine treatment engagement and skill utilization in adolescent ADHD, drawing on findings from a systematic review of cognitive-behavioral interventions that identifies common approaches for promoting engagement, research examining predictors of treatment engagement and differential treatment effects, and a school-based intervention augmented with novel mobile technology designed to support real-time skill use. Together, these findings illustrate opportunities to move beyond traditional approaches to intervention delivery by intentionally designing interventions to promote engagement, reinforce skill use, and provide support when and where adolescents need it. The presentation will highlight how engagement-focused strategies may enhance treatment response and will discuss implications for optimizing the delivery of ADHD interventions across school and outpatient settings. This presentation is relevant to mental health professionals, psychologists, clinicians, students, and trainees at an intermediate level. The speaker has reported no conflicts of interest or commercial support for this talk. Learning Objectives: Describe key components and common elements of cognitive-behavioral interventions for youth with ADHD.Evaluate the potential utility of digital tools for promoting real-time skill utilization and treatment engagement among adolescents with ADHD.At the conclusion of this presentation, participants will be able to: Analyze approaches for treatment engagement and factors associated with skill utilization among youth with ADHD.Apply research findings on treatment engagement and digital augmentation to identify opportunities for improving the delivery and effectiveness of ADHD interventions in clinical and school-based settings.Continuing Education: One hour of CE credit is available for attendees who are present for the entire program. We ask that all participants complete the given evaluation form at the conclusion of the program. The Center for Children and Families at FIU is approved by the American Psychological Association to sponsor continuing education for psychologists. The Center for Children and Families at FIU maintains responsibility for this program and its content. This free in-person talk has also been approved for up to 1 CEU credit by Florida Board of Clinical Social Work, Marriage and Family Therapy and Mental Health Counseling; and 1 CE credit by Florida Board of Psychology and Florida Office of School Psychology. Provider # BAP 50-12872. This event is proudly co-sponsored by the Department of Psychology.

events.title: Sacred Sound and Movement
events.host: Department of Religious Studies, Steven J Green School of International & Public Affairs
events.description: Ecstatic dance is the art of free movement—an invitation to surrender to rhythm and let music guide you inward. Much like meditation, it can open the door to altered states of awareness. Across cultures and traditions, dance has long been celebrated as a path to serenity, insight and connection with the divine. Many describe a profound sense of unity—with others, with the Earth and with their own inner being. Our journey begins by awakening life force through guided breathwork and visualization, gently preparing body and mind. From there, we flow into a spirited dance session led by a live DJ, allowing movement to carry us into expansion and joy. We then settle into stillness, immersed in the resonance of gong, quartz crystal bowls and ancient sound-healing instruments. This soundscape creates space for deep restoration, drawing on the timeless art of sound healing—where vibration itself becomes medicine, restoring balance throughout the body. Join us for this interactive experience exploring the transformative power of sacred sound and movement. As a special gift, each participant will receive a crystal gemstone to take home—a lasting reminder of the journey. Please bring a yoga mat and water bottle.

events.title: Writers on the Bay: Stacey Waite
events.description: The Writers on the Bay Reading Series presents Stacey Waite Stacey Waite is the Susan J. Rosowski Associate Professor of English at the University of Nebraska - Lincoln and is the author of five collections of poetry: Choke (winner of the Frank O’Hara Prize for Poetry), Love Poem to Androgyny, the lake has no saint (Winner of the Snowbound Prize for Poetry), Butch Geography (2013), and A Real Man Would Have A Gun (University of New Mexico Press, 2025). Waite is also the author of Teaching Queer: Radical Possibilities for Writing and Knowing (University of Pittsburgh Press, 2017). Working in both creative writing and composition studies, Waite is also co-editor of Inventing the Discipline: Student Work in Composition Studies and the textbook, Ways of Reading. Waite’s poetry and essays have appeared in such journals as Writing on the Edge, Assay, New Territory, Literacy in Composition Studies, and Black Warrior Review. Waite’s poems have been anthologized in a range of collections including Best American Poetry and The Norton Introduction to Literature. Waite's most recent collection was shortlisted for the Lambda Literary Award in LGBTQ+ Poetry. Visit Waite’s website at www.staceywaite.com.

events.host: College of Communication Architecture + The Arts, Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts
events.description: Pianist José López, Professor and Coordinator of the Piano Program at FIU, brings together four distinctive voices of the Romantic era in a program of rich contrasts. Schubert’s Sonata in A minor, D. 537, and selections from Liszt’s late piano works are presented alongside music by Charles-Valentin Alkan and Ferdinand Hiller’s Piano Sonata No. 2 in A-flat major, Op. 59. The program pairs celebrated composers with less familiar works, offering audiences a fresh perspective on the nineteenth-century piano repertoire. The program features Franz Schubert's Sonata in A minor (D. 537), a work by C.V. Alkan, Liszt's late piano works, and Ferdinand Hiller's Sonata Op. 59.

events.title: Beyond the Academic Paper: Writing Op-Eds For Policy Impact on Latin America
events.host: Kimberly Green Latin American and Caribbean Center
events.location: SIPA - School of International & Public Affairs
events.description: One of the most important components of an interdiscplinary education is learning how to conduct research and prepare academic papers. However, for those interested in working in policy, one of the most important skills that they can learn is how to distill the complex information learned through research into a condensed format that is more likely to be read by both policymakers and the general public— particularly through op-eds. This is particularly true for those that seek to influence policy—whether locally, nationally, or even globally—through their research. Navigating the op-ed writing and pitch process can, however, be daunting. This Op-Ed Writing Workshop will lay out the purpose and fundamentals of op-ed writing for policy audiences. Main topics or areas that will be covered: Writing for policy audiences, role for op-eds in the policy process, translating research and analysis into policy-relevant and impactful op-eds. Expected outcomes or skills participants will gain: Participants will learn how public writing can impact the policy-making process and the fundamentals of op-ed writing, pitching, and disseminating. Workshop Facilitator: Adam Ratzlaff, founder and CEO of Pan-American Strategic Advisors—a next-generation think tank and consulting firm focused on the Western Hemisphere—and a member of The Expert Network (TEN) with Diplomatic Courier's World in 2050. He has authored or co-authored over 150 public-facing and academic works on regional affairs, and his op-eds have been featured across local, national, and international outlets including Foreign Policy, The National Interest, LatinoAmerica21, Latinometrics, and Responsible Statecraft.

events.title: Sound of the Soul: An Introduction to the Bhagavad Gita
events.host: Department of Religious Studies, Steven J Green School of International & Public Affairs
events.description: Dr. Graham Schweig, a longtime scholar of comparative religion, offers a clear and welcoming introduction to the Bhagavad Gita, one of India’s great spiritual and philosophical texts. Set on the eve of a great battle, the Gita explores timeless questions of duty, action and the nature of the self. Its teachings have resonated with generations of readers around the world, including figures as diverse as Albert Einstein, Steve Jobs and Tupac Shakur. This talk is designed for students encountering the Gita for the first time, as well as those who already know it and want to go deeper. Join us for an accessible introduction to a text that has shaped global philosophy and spirituality for millennia.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival Opening Night: Amernet Performs Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 + Mendelssohn’s Octet
events.host: College of Communication Architecture + The Arts, Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts
events.description: The 2026 FIU Music Festival opens with an extraordinary anniversary performance celebrating 30 years of the Wertheim Performing Arts Center and the Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts. The Amernet String Quartet, FIU’s Artist-in-Residence ensemble, anchors an evening of masterworks, opening with Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 and continuing with Mendelssohn’s Octet, performed alongside Wertheim alumni and current students. Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto is brilliant, precise, and full of motion—an intricate conversation among instruments that still feels alive more than 300 years later. Mendelssohn’s Octet answers with youthful fire: sweeping, urgent, and astonishingly assured for a composer just sixteen years old. This milestone concert celebrates the full reach of Wertheim’s musical community: students beginning their professional journeys, alumni returning with the depth of experience, and faculty mentors whose leadership continues to shape the next generation. On one stage, past, present, and future come together in a powerful reflection of what the Wertheim has built over three decades. More than a festival opening, this performance is a celebration of excellence, mentorship, and community—a portrait of a living institution where talent is developed, relationships endure, and music continues to connect generations of musicians and audiences.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Toomai String Quintet
events.host: College of Communication Architecture + The Arts, Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts
events.description: Concert | 5:00 p.m. The FIU Music Festival welcomes the Toomai String Quintet for a program bringing together music, dance and the screen—including a suite from Carlos Rafael Rivera’s Grammy-winning score for the Netflix series The Queen’s Gambit. Formed at The Juilliard School, Toomai is known for crossing musical traditions and expanding the repertoire for string ensemble. Its commitment to Latin American music has led to more than 30 arrangements and commissions and two acclaimed recordings, Cuerdas Cubanas and Passos Brasileiros. The program places music by Pulitzer Prize-winning composer Tania León and Cuban composer and guitarist Leo Brouwer alongside works by three composers with deep ties to FIU: Distinguished University Professor Orlando Jacinto García and alumni Carlos Rafael Rivera ’96 and Marcus Norris ’17. Rivera’s Queen’s Gambit Suite draws from the score that earned him both Grammy and Emmy awards. A member of the School of Music’s first graduating class in 1996, Rivera has built an acclaimed career in film and television. Norris’s work spans concert music, opera, film and television, often bringing classical music into conversation with hip-hop, R&B and other contemporary traditions. The concert’s theatrical centerpiece is García’s prohibido (prohibited). Premiered at the New World Center in January 2025 by the New World Symphony with dancers from Miami City Ballet, the work returns in an intimate version for Toomai. Dancers Emily Bromberg and Alexander Sokolov of Dimensions Dance Theatre of Miami perform Ariel Rose’s choreography, with video by Jacek Kolasinski and John Stuart. Combining music, dance, video and spoken text in English and Spanish, prohibido confronts repression based on race, religion, beliefs, sexual orientation and other aspects of identity. The work reimagines García’s earlier string quartet I Never Saw Another Butterfly, written in memory of the children imprisoned at Terezín. Preconcert Conversation | 4:30 p.m. FIU alumni Carlos Rafael Rivera ’96 and Marcus Norris ’17 return to FIU for a special conversation with Orlando Jacinto García about their music, their connections to the university and careers spanning the concert hall, opera, film and television. Concert Program Tania León: Tumbao Marcus Norris: My Idols Are Dead Leo Brouwer: Música incidental campesina Carlos Rafael Rivera: Queen’s Gambit Suite Orlando Jacinto García: prohibido (prohibited) Featuring dancers Emily Bromberg and Alexander Sokolov of Dimensions Dance Theatre of Miami Choreography by Ariel Rose Video by Jacek Kolasinski and John Stuart

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Vincent Dubois, organ (Notre-Dame de Paris) and Marie-Andrée Joerger, accordion
events.host: College of Communication Architecture + The Arts, Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts
events.description: A rare musical encounter comes to Miami when Vincent Dubois, titular organist of Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, and internationally acclaimed accordion virtuoso Marie-Andrée Joerger bring their organ-and-accordion duo to FIU for their first official U.S. tour together. Performed on the Sydell Ida Wertheim Concert Organ, this FIU Music Festival program reimagines music of sweeping color, elegance and dance through an unexpected pairing of instruments capable of both grandeur and intimacy. The evening opens with Khachaturian’s brilliant Masquerade Waltz before moving through the refined French sound world of Debussy’s Petite Suite, Fauré’s Dolly Suite and Poulenc’s Suite française. Bartók’s Romanian Folk Dances adds earthy rhythm and folk-inspired vitality, leading into the modern pulse of Patrice Caratini’s La valse des crayons. For Miami audiences, the program’s tango-infused finale offers a special charge: Richard Galliano’s Tango pour Claude and Piazzolla’s Invierno Porteño and La Muerte del Ángel bring the evening to a close with music of elegance, tension and unmistakable dramatic force. Inventive, virtuosic and deeply atmospheric, this concert reveals the organ and accordion in thrilling conversation—expanding familiar repertoire into something fresh, vivid and entirely unexpected.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Liszt & Jiménez: Piano, Song, and Virtuosity
events.host: College of Communication Architecture + The Arts, Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts
events.description: Celebrate Franz Liszt’s birthday with pianists Kemal Gekić and José López and guest soprano Sonya Baker in a festival concert spanning solo piano, chamber music and song. The program pairs Liszt’s solo works with music by Afro-Cuban composer and virtuoso pianist José Manuel Jiménez (1852–1917). López presents Jiménez’s solo piano works and two chamber compositions, while Baker—who made her Carnegie Hall debut with conductor Michael Tilson Thomas—joins him for a selection of Lieder. FIU Artist-in-Residence and longtime Miami International Piano Festival artist Kemal Gekić brings his celebrated command of Liszt to the composer’s solo piano works. His performances and recordings have earned international acclaim, including the Rosette Award from The Penguin Guide to Classical Recordings for his recording of the Rossini-Liszt transcriptions. Presented in collaboration with the South Florida Chapter of the American Liszt Society, the concert places a towering figure of the Romantic era alongside a compelling Afro-Cuban voice deserving of wider recognition.

Lindsay Garritson and Ukrainian-born pianist Anastasiya Naplekova come together in a program featuring works composed by Weber alongside music inspired by his enduring influence. Garritson has appeared at Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center and earned top honors at major international piano competitions. Naplekova, praised for her “effortless virtuosity,” is a laureate of the Olga Kern, Hilton Head, Paderewski and Horowitz international piano competitions. Moving between dazzling solo showcases and the excitement of two pianists performing together, the program reveals Weber’s gift for drama, lyricism and brilliant keyboard writing—and the music his legacy inspired across generations. Experience two formidable pianists in an exhilarating celebration of Weber and his musical legacy at The Wertheim, an All-Steinway School.

events.description: Tuesday Times Roundtable TTR is FIU’s weekly series of moderated conversations around current global issues and trends. Register at go.fiu.edu/ttronline TTR: Leadership and Personal Branding in a Tech-Saturated Era Presenters: Carla Zensen, Senior Program Coordinator, Kopenhaver Center for the Advancement of Women in Communication, FIU CARTADr. Julie Hynes, Communication Studies Professor & Director of the Kopenhaver Center for the Advancement of Women in Communication, Rowan UniversityMarian Chia-Ming Liu, Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and media leader, Washington Post, CNN, & major national newsroomsSDG Topic Category: SDG 5: Gender EqualityNews Article: https://go.fiu.edu/ttr1103 Description: Professionals today are working through a media and technology landscape that keeps expanding. This panel brings together two experienced leaders in journalism and communications to talk about how they navigate that saturation while staying authentic to their own voice and work. events.title: Chris Gray Memorial Lecture - Imagine Lagos: Mapping New Perspectives on a Nineteenth-Century African City
events.host: African & African Diaspora Studies Program, Steven J Green School of International & Public Affairs
events.description: Urban questions have taken on a new urgency, as cities like Lagos grow faster and more intensely, seemingly every day. But how should we understand the ways the past shaped and produced this present? And how can, or should we, write and map the histories of people rooted in oral cultures? This presentation explores the premise that reading Lagos’s streets shapes the ways to ask, analyze and frame nineteenth-century narratives of the city. By drawing new maps of Lagos and the lagoon, I transcribe the answers to these questions as they were understood and framed in the city’s social geography.

events.title: Book Presentation and Conversation: To the Success of Our Hopeless Cause
events.host: Steven J Green School of International & Public Affairs, Václav Havel Program for Human Rights & Democracy
events.description: Join the Green School for a book presentation and conversation featuring To the Success of Our Hopeless Cause: The Many Lives of the Soviet Dissident Movement by Dr. Benjamin Nathans, who will be joined by historians Carlos Eire and Rebecca Friedman. Beginning in the 1960s, the Soviet Union was challenged by a dissident movement that captured the world’s imagination. Against all odds, these courageous individuals undermined the fearsome Soviet system and helped hasten its collapse three decades later. Taking its title from a toast offered at dissident gatherings, Dr. Nathans’s book tells the story of a remarkable group of people whose moral courage helped change the world. Their activism inspired movements in other totalitarian regimes, including Castro’s Cuba. Despite the island’s distance from the Soviet Union—geographically and culturally—the parallels between the Soviet and Cuban dissident movements are striking. This event explores a powerful story of hope and the enduring supremacy of human dignity over tyranny.

events.title: Documentary Film Screening: Symphony of Courage
events.host: Steven J Green School of International & Public Affairs, Václav Havel Program for Human Rights & Democracy
events.description: Five years ago, the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan, dramatically transforming life across the country and once again imposing severe restrictions on music and artistic expression. Join us for a screening of Symphony of Courage, a Voice of America documentary film that tells the remarkable story of the Afghanistan National Institute of Music, which was forced to close in August 2021 as its students and musicians faced persecution. The film follows sisters Farida and Zohra as they live in hiding under Taliban rule while the institute’s founder, Dr. Ahmad Sarmast, works with renowned cellist Yo-Yo Ma and others to secure safe passage for the school’s students, including members of its all-female orchestra. Their eventual escape to Lisbon, Portugal, is a powerful story of courage, resilience and the enduring freedom found through artistic expression. Following the film, join a conversation with president of the Friends of the Afghanistan National Institute of Music and COO of The Julliard School Lesley Rosenthal, and filmmaker Beth Mendelson, for a closer look at the mission to save the institute's students and the power of art to endure even in exile.

events.host: Benjamin León, Jr. Family Center for Geriatric Research and Education at FIU Seminar Series on Aging and Health, Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine
events.description: Safwan Badr, M.D., MBA, is a leading expert in sleep-disordered breathing. His research has focused on advancing the understanding of sleep apnea pathophysiology and applying those insights to develop innovative treatments. Badr chaired the workgroup that developed the American Academy of Sleep Medicine's clinical practice guideline for the treatment of central sleep apnea in adults. He is professor and chair of medicine at Wayne State University and serves on the board of directors of the American Board of Internal Medicine. Lunch will be provided. events.title: FIU Symphony Orchestra and Choirs: Bach’s Magnificat
events.host: College of Communication Architecture + The Arts, Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts
events.description: Experience the brilliance, dramatic energy, and expressive power of J.S. Bach live in Miami. Written during Bach’s first year in Leipzig and later revised into the D-major version known today, the Magnificat opens with trumpets, timpani, orchestra, and five-part chorus in a burst of radiant sound. Across twelve concise movements, Bach moves from festive choruses to intimate solo arias, shaping Mary’s song of praise with vivid word painting, rhythmic urgency, and remarkable emotional range. Conducted by Javier José Mendoza, the FIU Symphony Orchestra and Choirs bring together chorus, vocal soloists, and orchestra for a major School of Music performance. It offers South Florida audiences an evening of Bach at his most vivid: grand in scale, rich in feeling, and immediate in impact.
